articles.author: Renato Marinho
articles.description:
Large Language Models are notoriously bad at arithmetic and temporal logic. While they excel at linguistic nuance, asking an agent to calculate a US federal court filing deadline is essentially inviting a hallucination into your workflow. Even with sophisticated prompting, the model struggles with the intersection of arbitrary integer offsets (like '21 days') and the non-linear reality of human calendars—weekends and federal holidays.
A lawyer or a paralegal doesn't just need to add 21 to a date; they need to navigate a landscape of statutory rules, bank holidays, and weekend shifts. If an AI agent miscalculates a single deadline due to a missed Independence Day or a Sunday roll-over, the consequence isn't just a bug; it is professional negligence.
To solve this, we move the computation ou…

Introduction
Building web applications has become easier than ever. With the rise of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, and Cursor, developers can now generate code, create websites, and build functional applications simply by describing what they want.
This has given rise to a popular approach known as vibe coding.
Vibe coding involves using AI to generate code through natural-language instructions, sometimes with little attention to understanding how the code actually works.
Although this approach saves time and makes development more accessible, it also raises an important question: Are we building reliable software, or are we simply building applications that look good and work temporarily?
This is where software engineering becomes important.
